tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Search Spanish companies by name in the BORME registry. Returns ranked matches (fuzzy — tolerant of typos) with status and a mapasocietario.es/empresa link to cite. A hit's `name` is always its CURRENT registered name; when the entity has been renamed, `former_names` lists its prior name(s) — a hit

tools.name: get_company
tools.description: Get the BORME registry profile of one Spanish company: status, incorporation, current and former officers, sole shareholder (BORME records only sole-shareholder ownership), and — where available — NIF, share capital and registered address. NIF is never in BORME, and capital/address are missing for e

tools.name: search_officers
tools.description: Find a person (administrator/director/apoderado) in the BORME registry and list the companies they are linked to. Answers 'is officer Z present in other companies?'. tools.name: get_company_network
tools.description: Show companies directly connected to one Spanish company: via a shared board/management officer (shared_officer — apoderados and representatives are excluded as low-signal), via being owned by it (owns), or via owning it (owned_by). Answers 'is there a relationship between company X and company Y?'.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_company" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_officers · Private data: get_company · Public sink: get_company, search_officers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_officers · Private data: get_company · Public sink: get_company, search_officers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
